Source: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/notebooks/widgets
Fetched: 2026-06-17

Main heading:
"Input widgets allow you to add parameters to your notebooks and dashboards. You can add a widget from the Databricks UI or using the widget API."

== Widget types ==

- text: "Input a value in a text box"
- dropdown: "Select a value from a list of provided values"
- combobox: "Combination of text and dropdown. Select a value from a provided list or input one in the text box"
- multiselect: "Select one or more values from a list of provided values"

== Creating widgets ==

Python:
```python
dbutils.widgets.dropdown("state", "CA", ["CA", "IL", "MI", "NY", "OR", "VA"])
```

Scala:
```scala
dbutils.widgets.dropdown("state", "CA", Seq("CA", "IL", "MI", "NY", "OR", "VA"))
```

R:
```r
dbutils.widgets.dropdown("state", "CA", list("CA", "IL", "MI", "NY", "OR", "VA"))
```

SQL:
```sql
CREATE WIDGET DROPDOWN state DEFAULT "CA" CHOICES SELECT * FROM
(VALUES ("CA"), ("IL"), ("MI"), ("NY"), ("OR"), ("VA"))
```

"The widget API in SQL is slightly different but equivalent to the other languages."

== Accessing widget values ==

Python/Scala/R:
```python
dbutils.widgets.get("state")
dbutils.widgets.getAll()
```

SQL:
```sql
SELECT :state
```

== Removing widgets ==

Python/Scala/R:
```python
dbutils.widgets.remove("state")
dbutils.widgets.removeAll()
```

SQL:
```sql
REMOVE WIDGET state
```

== Widget restrictions ==

"Widgets only accept string values."

== SQL parameter markers ==

"Parameter markers protect your code from SQL injection attacks by clearly separating provided values from the SQL statements."

Requires: Databricks Runtime 15.2 and above

Examples:
```sql
SELECT :state

SHOW TABLES IN IDENTIFIER(:database)

SELECT * FROM IDENTIFIER(:database || '.' || :table) WHERE col == :filter_value LIMIT 100
```

DDL string clauses (DBR 18.0+):
```sql
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE my_table USING DELTA LOCATION :path
```
For DBR 14.3-17.3 LTS: use EXECUTE IMMEDIATE instead.

== Execution behaviors (widget on-change action) ==

1. "Run Notebook": "Reruns the entire notebook every time you select a new value."
2. "Run Accessed Commands": "Reruns only cells that retrieve the values for that particular widget every time you select a new value. This is the default setting when you create a widget. SQL cells are not rerun in this configuration."
3. "Do Nothing": "Does not rerun anything when you select a new value."

== Dashboard integration ==

"When you create a dashboard from a notebook with input widgets, all the widgets display at the top. In presentation mode, every time you update the value of a widget, you can click the Update button to re-run the notebook and update your dashboard with new values."

== %run parameter passing ==

"If you run a notebook that contains widgets, the specified notebook is run with the widget's default values."

Cluster-attached notebooks:
%run /path/to/notebook $X="10" $Y="1"

NOT available for SQL warehouses.

== UI widget configuration ==

Via "Edit > Add parameter". Dialog fields:
- Parameter Name — identifier used in code
- Widget Label — optional display name shown above widget
- Type
- Default value
- Possible choices (for dropdown/combobox/multiselect)
